facts.raw_span: prior percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction 2 months earlier
40‐year smoking history but had quit after his myocardial infarction
four episodes of bloody diarrhea daily
plasma glucose rose from 258 mg/dL to 449 mg/dL
Contrast‐enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography demonstrated swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct

support_spans: Contrast‐enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography demonstrated swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct
plasma glucose rose from 258 mg/dL to 449 mg/dL
hemoglobin A1c increased from 7.3% to 8.0%
contradict_spans: Anti–glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies were negative
concepts.why: The patient's pancreatic swelling and elevated serum amylase and lipase suggest pancreatitis, while the absence of anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies and the presence of extensive ulcerative colitis may indicate an autoimmune component.

concepts.preferred_label: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Pancreatic Involvement
support_spans: 3‐year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus
plasma glucose rose from 258 mg/dL to 449 mg/dL
hemoglobin A1c increased from 7.3% to 8.0%
contradict_spans: Contrast‐enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography demonstrated swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct
concepts.why: The patient's long-standing type 2 diabetes and recent worsening of glycemic control may be related to pancreatic involvement, but the imaging findings suggest a more complex pancreatic process.

support_spans: newly diagnosed extensive ulcerative colitis
four episodes of bloody diarrhea daily
contradict_spans: denied abdominal pain or fever
concepts.why: The patient's newly diagnosed ulcerative colitis and symptoms of bloody diarrhea are consistent with this diagnosis, but the absence of abdominal pain and fever is atypical.

support_spans: Contrast‐enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography demonstrated swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct
contradict_spans: plasma glucose rose from 258 mg/dL to 449 mg/dL
concepts.why: The patient's pancreatic swelling and imaging findings are consistent with chronic pancreatitis, but the recent worsening of glycemic control suggests a more complex process.

support_spans: Contrast‐enhanced CT and MR cholangiopancreatography demonstrated swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct
Serum IgG4 was 36.0 mg/dL
contradict_spans: Anti–glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies were negative
concepts.why: The patient's pancreatic swelling, elevated IgG4 levels, and absence of anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies suggest IgG4-related disease, but the diagnosis requires further confirmation.

It explains the uncovered finding of a prior percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction 2 months earlier in the context of the patient's current pancreatic symptoms and elevated serum IgG4 levels.

rationales.F05: Newly diagnosed extensive ulcerative colitis suggests extraintestinal manifestations.
rationales.F07: Bloody diarrhea is a common symptom of ulcerative colitis.
rationales.F12: Swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct is indicative of autoimmune pancreatitis and IgG4-related pancreatitis.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim and slight narrowing of the main pancreatic duct along with elevated Serum IgG4 levels decided it
